A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 24 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments measuring entropy across pretraining checkpoints, continual knowledge acquisition and forgetting, and memory-vector resuscitation, with additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the checkpoint comparisons, resuscitation experiments, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The resuscitation procedure is unchanged. Algorithm 1 replaces quant(C, p) with percentile(C, p), clarifying the already stated lowest-p-percent selection rule; the scaling formula and weight update remain identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use Dolma, PubMed, C4, Fictional Knowledge, and the same six downstream tasks. The appendix scenarios, including once versus paraphrased knowledge injection, are retained.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain the same unmodified-model comparisons, checkpoint comparisons, and attention-layer versus feed-forward-layer resuscitation comparisons. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Model configurations, data quantities, injection schedules, evaluation metrics, and batch-size, learning-rate, and epoch settings are unchanged. The corrected table references in Appendix B.4.2 do not revise experimental settings.

E4.justification: Appendices A–B retain the same analyses of datasets, activation functions, layers, injection frequency, hyperparameters, Pythia dynamics, resuscitation parameters, pretraining stages, and attention-layer resuscitation. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the Section 4.3 footnote reporting Pearson correlations of 0.94 and -0.96 with p-values of 6e-5 and 1e-5. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting information is added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the empirical figures retain their numerical entries and plotted results. For example, Table 1 baseline acquisition remains 25.2% at 118k and 18.8% at 738k. No result series or experimental outcome is added or removed.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, the entropy definitions, and the gradient argument in Appendix A.1 are unchanged. The threshold-function relabeling in Algorithm 1 does not change its mathematical selection criterion.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about declining knowledge entropy, its relationship to acquisition and forgetting, benefits from resuscitation, and the suitability of mid-stage checkpoints.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 replaces persistence at final-stage checkpoints, mentioning 554k, with consistency across pretraining checkpoints. This broadens the main-text summary, although unchanged Appendix B.7 and Section 6 still report worse end performance when resuscitating initial- and mid-stage models.

D1.justification: The implementation disclosures, optimizer and scheduling details, sequence length, preprocessing instructions, and code/data access information are retained. Algorithm 1's clearer function name adds no previously missing procedural detail.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 2 are unchanged. The reference list starts on a different page, but its membership is retained.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited grammar and punctuation corrections, clarifies Algorithm 1's wording, and corrects Appendix B.4.2 references from Table 2 to Table 1. It also updates the publication header and expands funding acknowledgments; the section structure remains stable.

P2.justification: Figures 11–12 receive small caption edits, and Table 1's caption changes capitalization. Expanded acknowledgments cause local spacing changes and move the reference-list opening from page 10 to page 11. The figures, axes, legends, and table structures are otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Appendix B.4.2's pointers to the actual acquisition/forgetting table and clarifying the percentile operation make the paper easier to follow. The broader checkpoint wording in Section 4.3 is less qualified, but the explicit failure conditions remain in Appendix B.7 and Section 6. Overall, the revision provides a small editorial improvement without strengthening the scientific evidence.
